notes: A silent mortal is pulled into the void on the ninth MUD hour (timer > IDLE_TO_VOID 8, one check per point_update). Any command from a voided player returns them to their room with "$n has returned." to that room's other occupants only (act TO_ROOM excludes the actor); the scenario's look proves C's return byte for byte (R1).

At sunset C loads the moon-matched blue portal and opens one ghost-ship dock/ship exit pair; sunrise removes them. Each send_to_room message reaches only awake players in its source room. DP-1316 (R1/R3/R4).

Eight MUD hours of silence stay on the near side of the threshold: check_idling compares timer > IDLE_TO_VOID (8), so the void lands on the ninth point_update and not the eighth. The immortal peer's own look at the eighth hour still lists the actor in the room and no departure act has appeared (R1/R3).

The voided player's departure is act("$n disappears into the void.", TO_ROOM) in the room they are leaving, emitted before the move to Limbo (char_to_room(ch, 1)). The same-room immortal peer receives exactly that line; the actor receives only its own "pulled into a void" line. DP-1311 put the port's room line back on game.Act so the transfer can no longer swallow it (R1/R4).

A command dequeued for a voided character returns them to GET_WAS_IN before dispatch and emits act("$n has returned.", TO_ROOM) in that room (comm.c:607). The peer sees exactly that line; the returnee never receives its own return message (R1/R2).

Per-recipient bytes for the whole void round trip: the actor sees only "You have been idle, and are pulled into a void." on the ninth tick, and the room peer sees only "$n disappears into the void." and later "$n has returned."; neither audience receives the other's line (R1).

An accepted command line resets char_specials.timer at the game-loop dequeue point, before dispatch, so eight further silent hours leave the player in the room and the void arrives on the ninth hour after the command, not the ninth hour of the session. The ~dpclock control line is consumed before C's input queue (comm.c:2027) and therefore must not reset the timer. DP-1311 restored the reset at the seam both transports share (R1/R2).

C moves the still-connected idler with char_to_room(ch, 3), whose room argument is an RNUM: with the shipped zone order rnum 3 is vnum 4 ("Frontline's Sphere"), so close_socket's act("$n has lost $s link.") reaches vnum 4's occupants. The port's PlayerTransfer(p, 3) resolves a VNUM, so its act reaches vnum 3 ("A Totally Empty Room"). A peer placed in each room exposes it both ways. The harness half of this vehicle is fixed (the deferred ~dpclock pump runs lifecycle-idle-force-rent-close green); what remains is F1, a production-fidelity fix, so this row stays blocked (R1/R5e).

The connected branch calls close_socket inside check_idling and NULLs ch->desc, so C never returns the character to the menu. The harness compares the server-initiated close as a <CLOSE> marker line; C and the port both close at the same pumped hour. The old ~dpclock seam pumped heartbeats inside process_input, so this same run freed the descriptor the input iteration still held and aborted the oracle with FD_SETSIZE; with the pump deferred to the game-loop heartbeat phase the run is byte-identical (R1/R5a).

Because C frees the descriptor before extract_char, extract_char_final's "hand the connection back to the menu" arm never runs for an idle force-rent: the terminal block carries <CLOSE> and no menu bytes on either engine, and the menu appears only after the closing <RELOGIN> re-enters the game (R1/R4).

After the forced disconnect the character comes back through the menu and re-enters from the rent file (free_rent is YES, config.c:106): the <RELOGIN> transcript, look, inventory and equipment bytes match the port. Persistence internals stay Go-test territory (R5f).

The deterministic-clock control only queues pulses; the game loop drains them at the production heartbeat slot, after descriptor input, command, output, prompt and CON_CLOSE processing. The seam's own contract (control queues without running a heartbeat, the drain yields the count exactly once, an over-cap control is refused without wrapping, non-DP_CLOCK controls stay ordinary input) is executed by DP_SEAM_SELFTEST and asserted in internal/oraclediff/seam_test.go (R3/R5a).

C queues the terminal hour's outdoor line and close_socket discards it (comm.c:2092 runs before the game loop's output pass, comm.c:636), so a C player never sees it; the port flushes it to the socket before retiring the session.
